thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - us-central-spot-gpu-pool exhaustion detected. queue length trending up 5m -> 3.2k, request failure rate 8% (gpu OOM / no capacity). Auto-scale attempted but hit provider CPU/GPU quota limits. Paging oncall.
Maya Chen: I'm on it, joining bridge. where is the impact? any customer-facing errors yet?
Samir Patel: most requests are getting queued; some requests are timing out at our proxy layer (504s). No broad 5xx yet but throughput is ~30% of steady-state.
Alejandro Ruiz: cloud console shows preemptible eviction spike in us-central-1b and most fallback pools are already saturated. Autoscaler logs: "scale_up_failed: quota_exceeded" for non-spot nodes as well.
Priya Rao: Confirming — autoscaler retried 3x then stopped. Policy: don't exceed committed budget for on-demand without explicit approval.
Lucy Park: Support: handful of high-volume customers reporting degraded latency on embeddings endpoints. We've opened temporary priority routing requests for two customers. Need ETA for mitigation.
Maya Chen: Quick mitigation plan: 1) spin up temporary `dedicated-burst` nodes (non-spot) in us-central-1c (manual) 2) lower default concurrency per-GPU to reduce OOMs 3) enable fallback model variants (quantized) for low-priority traffic 4) surface status update to customers.
Jordan Li: Product: we should throttle batch sizes and ensure we don't silently change outputs for paid customers. Prioritize correctness for paying customers, fallback for anonymous/free traffic.
Alex Kim: I'll take oncall handoff in 10m. Maya, can you run the manual node spin-up? I can approve billing bump.
Maya Chen: Starting manual provisioning: `gcloud compute instances create --machine-type a2-highgpu-1g ... --preemptible=false --labels=incident=2271234567` (starting with 4 nodes).
ops-bot: deploy request accepted. Provisioning job queued: job-id=prov-2271, estimated 6-8 minutes.
Samir Patel: Meanwhile lowering runtime concurrency from 32 -> 16 for all L0 pools to reduce per-request memory. Applying patch to config: `CONCURRENCY_L0=16` and reloading router.
Alejandro Ruiz: Applying fallback routing: update list to include `model-x-q4_0` for non-paid traffic. Patch sent to routing service: `PATCH /routing/v1/fallbacks` payload: "{ \"priority\": \"free\", \"fallback\": \"model-x-q4_0\" }".
Lucy Park: Sent initial customer note: "We're aware of increased latency for inference in US-C, teams are working on restoring capacity. We'll update in 15 minutes."
Maya Chen: Provisioning logs: `prov-2271` nodes came up 5m 12s after start, kube nodes registered. Starting drain push for queued pods onto new nodes.
Samir Patel: Queue is decreasing but still ~900. Observed a secondary failure: some pods crash-looping with OOM when migrated to new nodes due to a different TF runtime. Rolling restart with updated container (reduced max_batch) to mitigate.
Alex Kim: Handoff: I'm primary now. Maya stay on infra, Samir you own runtime tweaks, Alejandro watch autoscaler/quotas, Priya keep billing approvals flowing, Lucy keep customers updated, Jordan coordinate priorities.
Priya Rao: Approved temporary quota bump for on-demand GPUs for up to 12 hours. Notifying finance.
Alejandro Ruiz: Autoscaler metrics: backlog dropping from 3.2k -> 420 over 18 mins after nodes and concurrency change. However provider reports new preemption wave incoming in 1-2h for spot pools. We should ensure fallback remains active.
Samir Patel: Pushed conservative backoff/retry policy to SDK: `retry_policy: { max_attempts: 2, base_delay_ms: 300 }` to avoid amplifying queue. Also disabled speculative prefetching on embeddings workload.
Maya Chen: Also turned on short-term KV prefix cache for model kvs to reduce token compute for retries.
Lucy Park: Support update: customers on SLO tier see improved latency for priority routes. Free-tier still intermittent, adding note to status page.
ops-bot: statuspage update queued: "Partial degradation in US-C affecting free-tier inference; paid customers prioritized. Next update in 15m."
Jordan Li: Product request: capture sample outputs from the quantized fallback and run quick eval on the known prompt suite for two top customers before broad rollout. Samir, can you run that?
Samir Patel: Running evals now; initial diff looks acceptable for embedding similarity (<2% drift) but generation quality drops for specific prompts. We'll gate fallback to non-generation endpoints immediately.
Maya Chen: Action summary so far: 4 non-spot nodes added, concurrency halved, fallback model enabled for free-tier embeddings only, SDK retry/backoff tightened, support notified. Queue down to ~120.
Alex Kim: Good. Next actions: 1) Monitor preemption alerts, 2) if provider signals further spot evictions, flip route to other region (us-west2) for non-SLA traffic, 3) prepare rollback plan for any user-facing regression.
Alejandro Ruiz: Opening cross-region routing change now but it's low priority until we see more evictions. Need approval for cross-region bandwidth — Priya?
Priya Rao: Approved temporary inter-region traffic for incident window.
Lucy Park: Crafting customer follow-up: will call out root cause (spot preemptions + provider quota), what we did (manual nodes + routing + throttles), and ETA for full normalization ~2-4 hours.
Samir Patel: Note: we saw a small number of model shards fail to recover due to kube taints during provisioning; patched tolerations and restarted DaemonSet on new nodes. No data loss.
Maya Chen: Current numbers: queue 54, error rate 0.6%, steady-state throughput ~85% pre-incident. Keeping this thread open until fully recovered and postmortem assigned.
ops-bot: incident recorded: ID INC-2271234567, severity=SEV2, pageresolve ETA=2h.
Alex Kim: I'll escalate to oncall+eng-sre for postmortem. Thanks team — keep updates inline.
Lucy Park: Posted status update to customers with link to support ticket for impacted accounts.
Samir Patel: One last note — recommend changing autoscaler fallback policy to allow a controlled spend increase for 15 minutes if queue > 500 in the future. Filing RFC now.
Maya Chen: Acknowledged. Updating runbook with today's manual steps. Ending primary mitigation actions; monitoring.
incident-bot: Update: incident remains open. Next automated check-in in 15m.
